C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF.Summary: Make the M-045 extension edit pipeline honest about its outcome: the two dead unbound insertion routes (POST /ext/text-insert and the mt_ext_text_insert/mt_ext_text_transform commands) refuse at the source instead of answering success for events the editor targeting gate always drops; /ext/apply validates operations before emitting, gains a bounded renderer ack channel, and answers by the actual application fact instead of an unconditional applied:true; apply batches become idempotent by an optional client request id backed by a bounded server dedup; and the outbound invoke carries a stable Idempotency-Key across its internal retries, honors Retry-After with a bounded wait, while Mark's own budget 429 starts sending Retry-After.
C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF.Problem: Verified against the current worktree (branch spec/ext-edit-proof, base bb68fd6c); wave-2 scout findings 1, 2, 3, 11, 17, 19 share one cause: the edit pipeline is fire-and-forget with no result channel and no idempotency, and its three insertion routes carry divergent binding contracts of which two are dead. (1) POST /ext/text-insert (live_server.rs:1542-1587) authenticates via authenticate_incoming (1547), builds a payload without any document binding — json!({"text": req.text, "position": null}, 1557-1560) — emits mt::text::op (1568) and answers {"ok": true} (1583-1586). Since C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING the editor gate extBindingMatchesRendered (editor.vue:3388-3391) drops every unbound event fail-closed — the gate comment names /ext/text-insert and the text_ops.rs commands explicitly (editor.vue:3384-3386) — so the route answers ok:true for an insert that can never be applied; the same is true for the Tauri commands mt_ext_text_insert/mt_ext_text_transform (text_ops.rs:109-141, 148-178; payloads TextInsertPayload 120-123 and TextTransformPayload 158-160 carry no binding), which are registered as public commands (main.rs:971-972, m001_validate.rs:103-104) with no renderer caller in src. (2) POST /ext/apply (live_server.rs:1689-1811) passes the C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING binding fence (400 missing at 1705-1714, 409 mismatch at 1726-1735, zero events) but then emits each operation (1745-1796) and answers ExtApplyResponse {applied: true, operations_count: req.operations.len()} (1804-1810) unconditionally: the renderer's verdict never travels back — a gate cut after a tab switch between context and apply (editor.vue:3403-3407, 3432-3436, 3465-3469), or a Muya apply exception (editor.vue:3414-3417, 3454-3457), is swallowed while the extension already read applied:true. Unknown op_type strings are skipped with continue (1771-1776) yet still counted into operations_count (1806-1809) — operations that were neither validated nor applied are reported as applied. (3) No idempotency: ExtApplyRequest (live_server.rs:331-343) carries no request key, so a client retry after a lost response emits and applies the whole batch twice; the contrast inside the same file is /stream/patch's seq dedup, which short-circuits retransmits before validation and apply and answers duplicate:true (live_server.rs:1218-1240). (4) The outbound invoke (invoke.rs) has the same gap mirrored: InvokeRequest {capability, payload} (invoke.rs:58-62) carries no idempotency key while the client retries once on 503 (146-154) and once on connect errors (167-176) with a fixed 500 ms sleep (152, 174), so a processed-but-unacknowledged extension call repeats; Retry-After is absent from src-tauri entirely (repo grep empty). Mark's own budget rate refusal answers 429 with an error body and no Retry-After header (live_server.rs:1310-1328), so the honest-waiting signal is missing in both directions. The external-contract constraint is real: the sole external consumer of these routes is TokMo, which this repo cannot update in lockstep — the C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES disposition records no supported production text-insert caller in the inspected TokMo revision and preserves Mark's v1 {text, source} request body (.grace/changes/archive/C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES/paired-client-disposition.md:12, plan.xml:432) — so request shapes must not change, but today's ok:true and applied:true answers are provably false and no compatibility argument can save them.
C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF.Relationship: Lineage, all landed: C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING built the authoritative binding fence and the editor targeting gate — this change preserves their semantics byte-for-byte in meaning (400 missing / 409 mismatch before any event, never applied:true on refusal; the gate stays the single fail-closed authority) and adds the missing fact channel on top of an already-fenced pipeline. C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND (#298) made every route authorize by the stored grant — untouched; the capability gate still runs first on every route here. C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND and C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH are untouched. C-STREAM-BUDGET owns the /stream/* refusal semantics — its budgets, statuses, bodies and tests keep their meaning; the only touch is the additive Retry-After header on the existing rate 429. C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES set the external wire disposition this change honors: request bodies stay v1 ({text, source} on /ext/text-insert), and the response-side corrections are justified below in Constraints because the current answers are demonstrably false. This bundle is one of four triaged from the 2026-11-22 wave-2 scout (B1 EXT-EDIT-PROOF; B2 trust-coherence, B3 gallery-state, B4 delivery-honesty are neighboring bundles) and closes the edit half of the wave-2 acceptance criterion: a successful confirmation corresponds to exactly one edit in the right tab, and on refusal the client sees the refusal.

Goals.Goal: The dead unbound routes refuse at the source. An authorized /ext/text-insert caller receives a non-2xx refusal (501 Not Implemented) whose body keeps the file's plain {"error": ...} voice with a stable machine reason naming the deprecated route and the live alternative (/ext/context read + /ext/apply) — no mt::text::op event is emitted, nothing reaches the renderer. The existing authentication/capability gate keeps running first, so the current refusal pins (no token, wrong token, disabled extension, missing capability — all 401 with zero events) keep their exact statuses. The Tauri commands mt_ext_text_insert and mt_ext_text_transform likewise refuse with a stable Err code in the existing string-code voice (ext_enable_reapproval_required precedent) without emitting; their names, signatures and allowlist entries stay.

/ext/apply answers by fact. Operation validation moves before any emission: an unknown op_type refuses the whole batch with 400 and zero events (the /stream/patch unknown-op precedent), so operations_count never counts unvalidated operations. Every emitted operation event carries a server-issued batch request id and its op index (additive optional payload fields, absent-field serialization preserved). After its binding gate decides, the renderer answers through one new additive Tauri event mt::ext::text_op_ack carrying {request_id, op_index, applied, reason}: an event cut by the gate nacks with a stable content-free reason; a Muya failure nacks with a stable failure class, never raw error text. The handler collects the verdicts under a bounded timeout (named constant, 5 s default — the same order as the /ext/context round trip at live_server.rs:1635) and answers 200 with {applied: true, operations_count} only when the whole batch is ack'd applied; a gate-cut or nack answers 409 with the plain error body naming the failed op index and whether earlier operations applied; a timeout or a missing renderer subscriber answers 504 with a stable reason (the /ext/context timeout precedent at 1674-1677). The binding fence and the capability gate are untouched and still precede everything.

/ext/apply becomes idempotent. The request gains an optional client request id (additive serde field): when present it is the idempotency key — the server keeps a bounded, process-local record of terminal verdicts keyed by extension id plus request id, a replay returns the recorded first verdict (same status, same body) with an additive duplicate marker and re-emits nothing, and a retry arriving while the first attempt is still awaiting its ack coalesces onto the pending verdict instead of emitting again (the /stream/patch duplicate:true vocabulary at 1218-1240). The dedup short-circuit runs after authentication and before the fence, so a replay never re-enters the document. When the client sends no key the server mints one for ack correlation only and makes no dedup promise — honest for the un-updatable external client, and no legacy caller is 400'd (an absent reliability key is not a fail-closed security condition, unlike an absent binding).

The outbound invoke is honest across retries. invoke_extension attaches an Idempotency-Key header that is generated per logical call and stays identical across its internal retry attempts (503 and connect-error), so a retried request is recognizable as the same operation by the extension; the retry policy honors a Retry-After header on 503 and 429 in place of the fixed 500 ms sleep, with the wait clamped to a bounded named ceiling (a hostile or broken header can never stall the invoke) and 429 joining the existing single-retry budget; the loopback-only, no-proxy, no-redirect, redirect-not-followed contract is unchanged.

Both directions of Retry-After become honest: Mark's budget rate 429 (live_server.rs:1310-1328) gains a Retry-After header derived from the bucket refill (integer seconds, bounded by the refill period), while budget semantics — zero mutation on refusal, last valid revision intact, dedup/resync short-circuits free — are unchanged; all other budget refusals keep their exact current responses.

After the refusal of the dead routes, the one live mutation contract is /ext/apply under the one binding gate: the divergence among insertion rules ends structurally, the deprecated routes are documented as refusing (module contracts and the refusal reasons say so), and the editor-side gate with its editor_ext_targeting suite remains the single fail-closed authority with its meaning intact.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact ObservedWriteScope, enumerated by reading the current tree:

Read-only anchors: src-tauri/src/main.rs (the LiveServerState literal stays untouched — the new pending-verdict and dedup state is process-global in live_server.rs exactly like EXT_DOCUMENT_BINDINGS/CONTEXT_REQUEST_COUNTER, whose own doc comment at live_server.rs:281-284 states that pattern's purpose), src-tauri/src/m045_ext/mod.rs (command signatures unchanged), registry.rs, auth.rs, live_bridge.rs, manifest.rs, discovery.rs, src-tauri/src/m001_validate.rs (allowlist names unchanged), src/renderer/src/components/extensionGallery/index.vue, src/renderer/src/store/editor.js, src/renderer/src/components/liveViewer/, the bootstrap-ipc shim and its listener pin (src/renderer/__tests__/bootstrap-ipc.test.js:142-151) — the ack event travels renderer-to-backend like mt::ext::context_response (editor.vue:3606-3617, Rust listener registered in start_live_server at live_server.rs:1949-1969), which needs no shim registration. live_bridge.rs is used as-is: mt::text::op is emitted via app_handle directly today and stays so.

Wire changes are additive on the request side and honesty-corrective on the response side, justified: (a) no request body changes — TextInsertRequest keeps {text, source} (C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES plan.xml:432), ExtApplyRequest gains only the optional request id and new fields deserialize-absent on legacy senders; (b) /ext/text-insert's {"ok": true} is replaced by a refusal because the answer is provably false today — the gate has dropped every unbound event since C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING (editor.vue:3384-3386 names this route), so no client has received a real insert on this route since 2026-11-20 and the sole external consumer cannot be updated in lockstep; a permanent truthful refusal beats a permanent lie; (c) /ext/apply keeps the response fields applied and operations_count with their names, but applied:true is only answered on 200 after the ack'd fact, operations_count only counts validated, verdict-backed operations, and every non-applied outcome is a non-2xx status with the file's plain error-body voice (the 400/409 fence vocabulary extended by 504) — a future TokMo integration records its compatible client version per the disposition precedent.

Names and channels: command names mt_ext_text_insert/mt_ext_text_transform, route paths, mt::text::op and mt::ext::context_request/response are unchanged; the only new channel is mt::ext::text_op_ack (renderer-to-backend); the only new wire fields are the additive ones named in the goals; the ack listener registers inside the existing SERVER_BOOT block next to the context_response listener.

Timing budgets are bounded and named: the apply ack timeout is a named constant defaulting to 5 s (same order as the /ext/context round trip); the invoke Retry-After wait clamps to a named ceiling of the same order as the current fixed sleep; the dedup record is bounded (capped recent entries, eviction policy is plan detail, process-local, cleared on restart) — no unbounded memory from either channel; a replay after a restart is not a dedup hit and is refused by the already-recorded-binding fence, which is acceptable and documented.

Security hygiene unchanged: no log line, error body or ack reason carries secret material or document content — ack and refusal reasons are stable content-free class strings in the BLOCK_ log voice; the loopback-only binding, Bearer model, capability gate order and grant enforcement are untouched; repository artifacts stay English and the GRACE surface (module contracts, CHANGE_SUMMARY entries, module maps, graph, verification) is synchronized with the implementation.

No new user-facing UI strings: every new client-visible text is a stable machine code for the extension client or a log marker; the gallery, its error surface and all ten locale files are out of scope, so the C-62 all-locales canon is not triggered by this change.

Predecessor suites keep meaning: the C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING binding matrix (tests.rs:1158-1250 — 400 missing, 409 mismatch/stale, zero events, context carries binding), the capability matrix and grant-bound pins of #298, the rebind and denial suites, C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH fencing and the C-STREAM-BUDGET suites (tests.rs:2055-2395) pass without weakened assertions or budgets. Exactly two pins move, named: text_insert_authorized_emits_with_requester_identity (tests.rs:1086-1094) and the emit leg of text_insert_authorized_old_shape_body_emits (tests.rs:1097-1105) move from "200 plus one event" to the honest refusal semantics while the old-shape body deserialization pin inside the latter keeps proving the v1 body still parses.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No gallery redesign or lifecycle work (scout keys 4, 13, 14, 15, 16 — bundle B3): discovery, register/enable flag preservation, toggle and list honesty stay untouched.

No disable/revoke/trust-coherence work (scout keys 5, 7, 8, 12 — bundle B2): no enabled-fence on in-flight data routes beyond what exists, no grant-overwrite dialog change, no revoke-retry rework; the fence-vs-disable race on /ext/apply remains bundle B2's.

No stream/endpoint delivery honesty work (scout keys 18, 20, 10 — bundle B4): no doc_open ack channel, no endpoint publication retry, and the unfiltered extension error body inside InvokeError.message (invoke.rs:155-165) stays as-is — only the key header and retry policy of invoke.rs change here.

No binding contract is added to /ext/text-insert: the alternative of teaching the route document_id/document_generation like /ext/apply is rejected because it would force a coordinated client update that this repo cannot perform (external TokMo, disposition precedent) or 400 every legacy caller, while the honest live path already exists as context-read-plus-apply; the route refuses and says so.

No retry expansion beyond the existing single retry: no general retry queue, no cross-restart dedup persistence, no batching/coalescing of multiple apply batches beyond same-key coalescing, no change to /stream/* dedup or budgets beyond the additive 429 header, no pairing or grant model change, no renderer-visible error surface for refusals beyond the existing log markers.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first route tests: an authorized /ext/text-insert request (valid bearer, enabled extension with text.insert) answers 501 with a stable machine reason and zero mt::text::op events, while the four existing gate refusals keep 401-class statuses with zero events and the v1 body still deserializes — today this exact request answers 200 with {"ok": true} and one emitted event (tests.rs:1086-1094 pins the old behavior), so the new assertions are red before the fix.

Failing-first command tests: mt_ext_text_insert and mt_ext_text_transform on a registered, enabled extension return the stable refusal code and emit no mt::text::op; a disabled or unregistered extension keeps the existing get_manifest refusal — today the enabled path returns Ok(()) and emits (text_ops.rs:109-141, 148-178), so the new assertions are red before the fix.

Failing-first op validation: an /ext/apply batch containing an unknown op_type answers 400 with zero emitted events and no applied:true — today it answers 200 with the unknown op counted into operations_count (live_server.rs:1771-1776, 1806-1809), so the new assertion is red before the fix.

Failing-first ack contract: an /ext/apply batch whose events carry the request id is answered 200 {applied: true, operations_count} only when the harness (the existing incoming_fixture context-responder pattern extended to the ack event) acks every op applied; a gate-cut or nack yields 409 with the reason naming the failed op index and the applied prefix; no ack within the budget yields 504; today the handler answers applied:true immediately after emit with no channel (live_server.rs:1785-1810), so every leg is red before the fix. Emit failure keeps the existing honest 500 branch.

Failing-first idempotency: two /ext/apply posts with the same request id emit the batch exactly once and the second response equals the recorded first verdict with the duplicate marker — including refusal verdicts — and a same-key post arriving while the first is pending coalesces without a second emit; different keys apply independently; a keyless post applies once with no dedup promise. Today there is no key and no dedup (tests.rs has no such test; the second post re-emits), so these are red before the fix.

Failing-first invoke tests, on the honest loopback harness (tests.rs:1799-1855): every attempt of one logical call carries the same Idempotency-Key; a 503 or 429 with Retry-After produces a bounded wait honoring the header (clamped to the ceiling) and 429 is retried once within the existing attempt budget; a Retry-After over the ceiling waits no longer than the ceiling. Today no key header exists, 429 is a terminal BadStatus, and the sleep is a fixed 500 ms — all red before the fix. The redirect-not-followed and loopback-refusal pins keep passing unchanged.

Failing-first 429 header: the budget rate refusal answers 429 with a Retry-After header of bounded integer seconds — today the header is absent (live_server.rs:1317-1327), and stream_budget_patch_refuses_over_rate (tests.rs:2124) gains the header assertion while every existing budget test keeps its status, body and zero-mutation semantics.

Failing-first renderer relay and gate verdicts: the textOps relay forwards request_id and op_index on the ext-text-insert/ext-text-transform/ext-undo bus emits (absent forwards undefined, current relay tests keep passing), and the editor_ext_targeting suite (editor-coverage.test.js:3076+) gains verdict pins — a matched apply emits one applied ack after the mutation, and the foreign/stale/null/absent binding cases emit a nack with the stable content-free reason while still refusing before any mutation — today no ack is emitted on any path, so these are red before the fix; an event without request_id behaves exactly as today with no ack.

All predecessor suites named in Constraints pass in meaning after the fix; the two moved text-insert pins are the only semantic moves and are called out in the plan; graph ownership, module maps and file-local contracts (M-045 live_server/text_ops/invoke, M-011 editor EXT_TEXT_OPS block, textOps relay) describe the final implementation, with module contracts carrying the honest-refusal and ack-channel documentation of the unified insertion contract.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The named failing-first behaviors — dead-route refusal (501, zero events, old body parses), command refusal (stable code, zero events), unknown-op 400 (zero events), ack verdict legs (200 applied / 409 nack with failed index / 504 timeout), key idempotency (single emit, recorded verdict, duplicate marker, in-flight coalescing), invoke key-and-Retry-After (stable key across attempts, bounded honored wait, 429 retried once), budget 429 Retry-After header — each fail before the fix and pass after it; the binding matrix, capability/grant matrix, rebind, stream-auth and budget suites pass unchanged in meaning; the two moved text-insert pins are named in the plan. No e2e suite covers the /ext data routes today (the only live e2e, live-stream-ownership.spec.ts, pins /stream ownership, which this change does not touch), so none is required; before archiving: grace lint --path . --change C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF --assertions final --run-commands, then grace lint --path . --assertions current and grace status --path . --with modules --json.

Assumptions.Assumption: TokMo is the sole external consumer and cannot be updated in lockstep (C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES disposition: no supported production text-insert caller identified in the inspected revision; existing context/apply consumers retain their declared protocol shapes) — the spec treats response-side honesty corrections as justified and request-side shapes as frozen; a future TokMo integration records its compatible client version before claiming support, per that precedent.

The apply ack subscriber is the same single webview that owns the rendered editor; a missing subscriber (listener torn down, webview closed, app quitting) manifests as ack timeout and therefore as the honest 504 — there is no multi-window fan-out to model.
The dedup record is process-local memory cleared on restart; replay-after-restart relies on the binding fence (the remembered binding dies with the process) and is accepted, not handled.

Approval of this draft specification approves neither an unwritten plan nor apply/archive, lane departure or release; the exact refusal status constants (501 for the deprecated route, 409/504 bodies), the ack timeout and dedup-cap values, and the Retry-After ceiling are plan-level constants within the bounds pinned here.
